title: Udyoga: the embassy, Krishna's counsel, Karna and Kunti
hook: Karna is at his prayers on the riverbank, facing the sun, and the woman waiting in his shadow is his mother.
carry: Udyoga: the embassy, Krishna's counsel, Karna and Kunti
tomorrow: Bhishma Parva (the Gita re-read in place, 6 sessions)

segments.voice: Yesterday, in the Udyoga book, Krishna offered Karna a throne, and Karna chose the mother who raised him. Your line was Udyoga: the embassy, Krishna's counsel, Karna and Kunti. Did you name the bond before you answered? Day eight hundred eighteen.

On the bank of the Ganga, a man stands with his face to the east and his hands raised, reciting his prayers. The sun climbs. It burns the back of his neck, and he doesn't move. Behind him, a woman has come quietly and stands in the shade of his own upper cloth. She waits until he is finished. It's Kunti, and the man is Karna. Yesterday, Krishna asked Karna to change sides. Today, his mother comes to ask the same thing, in person.
screen: `PRAYERS ON THE GANGA BANK` → `KUNTI WAITS IN HIS SHADOW` → `A MOTHER'S REQUEST`

segments.voice: Karna finishes, turns, and greets her by naming himself: I am Karna, son of Radha and Adhiratha. What can I do for you? Hear the sting in that, even if he doesn't intend one. Kunti tells him the truth. You are not a charioteer's son. You are mine, and the Sun's. Come to your brothers. In the text, a voice even speaks from the sun to confirm her words. Karna doesn't doubt her. But he answers her plainly, and it's hard to hear. You cast me away when I was born. You never gave me a mother's care. Now, on the eve of war, you come to me for the sake of your other sons. And then, after the hardest words, Karna gives her something. He will not join the Pandavas. But he makes a promise. In the battle, he will not kill four of her sons: Yudhishthira, Bhima, Nakula and Sahadeva, even when he has them at his mercy. Only Arjuna will he fight to the end. Either way, he says, you will still have five sons: with Arjuna, or with me. Kunti trembles and embraces him. She asks him to remember his promise, and they part. Look at what has happened in this chapter. The Udyoga book is the book of getting ready, and both sides use it to gather allies. Karna uses it to give away his advantage, out of love for a mother who gave him up. It's a gift, and it may cost him his life.
screen: `I AM KARNA, SON OF RADHA` · `YOU ARE MINE, AND THE SUN'S` · `FOUR BROTHERS SPARED, NOT ARJUNA` · then, large: `YOU WILL STILL HAVE FIVE SONS`

segments.voice: Settle where you are. Let your shoulders drop. Think of a conversation you've been putting off, one where the truth is hard and the love is real. You don't have to have it today. Just breathe with it. Breathing in, name the hard thing, silently. Breathing out, name the thing you could still give, even if you can't give everything. Stay there, between the two, the way Karna did on the riverbank. If you pray, you can bring that person into your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Udyoga. The book of getting ready. Our days with it end here, on choices made by a river, before the armies take the field.
Your line: Udyoga: the embassy, Krishna's counsel, Karna and Kunti. Today, in one place where you can't give everything, give the one thing you can. Day eight hundred eighteen.

fork.setup: you're Karna. your birth mother asks you to join your brothers on the eve of war. you've already refused Krishna. what do you do?
options: refuse her completely and send her away.
refuse, but promise to spare four of her sons.
fork.reveal: Karna stays with Duryodhana, but gives Kunti a promise: he will fight only Arjuna to the end, so she will still have five sons.

original.note: Karna, Kunti's first son, raised by the charioteer Adhiratha and his wife Radha.

trapdoor: what you thought: Kunti's visit failed.
what it means: Karna refused to switch sides, but promised to spare four of her sons.
what a scholar hears: the promise shapes what's coming: when Karna later has some of those brothers at his mercy, readers watch to see if he keeps it.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Udyoga Parva (Bhagavat-yana), Kunti meets Karna on the bank of the Ganga; Karna's reply and promise

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli: Karna at prayers facing east until the sun scorches his back; Kunti waiting in the shade of his upper garment; his greeting naming Radha and Adhiratha; the voice from the sun (Surya) confirming her words; his reproach; his promise to spare Yudhishthira, Bhima and the twins and fight only Arjuna; 'you will still have five sons'.

The word segment says our Udyoga days end here. In the full epic, the Udyoga Parva continues after this scene (e.g. the armies marching and the Amba story). Also confirm the gloss of udyoga as 'preparing / getting ready' (literally effort, exertion).
Trapdoor floor 3 points ahead to the Karna Parva; keep vague so as not to teach a future day.
